title: Pin the case-fold table digest: a test that fails on drift of unicode-case-folding (DEC-282 (a12) pair item)
description: DEC-282 (a12) (opum-doc, opum-ai/opum-doc#1870 family): the lore/quest pair shares one case-fold table, and a change to it is a pair change with a digest test failing in whichever half lags. lore pins the CASE_FOLD_TABLE_DATA string of its vendored, generated file (src/adapters/case-fold-table.ts; digest ef08b22d969b928737ae158c7a0d2bc4b800769b178f99db69f21bd68255fc13, each entry String.fromCodePoint(cp) plus String.fromCodePoint(...mapped), ascending, joined by "\n" with no trailing newline, hashed as UTF-8) and never reads the library. quest had no such test: unicode-case-folding is used only in src/domain/records.ts (caseFold), package.json (^1.1.1) and bun.lock, so a lockfile regen resolving 1.1.2 would silently diverge from lore. TEST ONLY: pin the fold data quest actually uses, in quest own representation (every code point 0..0x10FFFF, lookupFolding(cp) when defined, one line "<cp hex>:<mapped hex,...>\n", sha256; 1585 entries at 1.1.1, C+F statuses) AND build lore exact representation from the same runtime table and assert lore digest, so one shared constant is pinned in both repos. Do not change package.json or bun.lock (a dependency path needing a floor check first).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test pins the sha256 of the lookupFolding table of the installed unicode-case-folding (1585 entries at 1.1.1), stating exactly what it hashes
The test goes red when the table drifts (shown by a mutant that perturbs one entry or the entry count)
No change to package.json or bun.lock

plan: 1. Pin quest table in its own representation (digest bea3c0c9..., 1585 entries) - landed in round 1.

2. Round 2 (opus verdict, sha256 0a58aa155ebb3290a0d89d942bfb20e52fd4e08ffa8f62849e9e93e925e6026b, quest-773-verdict.txt): also build lore exact representation from quest runtime table and assert ef08b22d... (B1); measured: quest table produces it, no pair finding.
3. SF1: pin caseFold (the function src calls) against lookupFolding at every code point.
4. SF2: foldTable takes the lookup; wrappers altering one F entry and dropping one code point must move both digests; rename the test.
5. Nits: drop the surrogate skip, add the C+F comment, correct the description.
implementationNotes: Round 2 on opum-ai/quest-cli#773 (head a9d69ea6): REQUEST CHANGES, one blocker (B1 two self-pins, no shared constant), SF1, SF2, nits. Verdict file quest-773-verdict.txt in the opum-agent scratchpad, sha256 0a58aa155ebb3290a0d89d942bfb20e52fd4e08ffa8f62849e9e93e925e6026b. Measured at unicode-case-folding 1.1.1: quest runtime table in lore exact form hashes to ef08b22d969b928737ae158c7a0d2bc4b800769b178f99db69f21bd68255fc13 over 1585 entries, equal to lore pin, so no pair finding. Mutants shown red: lore pin one character off (pin test and drift test), wrapper made a no-op (drift test), caseFold-vs-table disagreement (caseFold test). The surrogate skip was dropped; no surrogate key exists, so the quest digest bea3c0c9... is unchanged.
